seo.title: Iconise — guided icon creation
seo.description: Iconise case study: guided app icon design, iteration history, configurable AI generation, and PNG, derived SVG and favicon exports.

hero.hook: From an app idea to a finished icon
hero.description: A guided studio to explore visual directions, retain design decisions, and refine an app icon through to export.

overview.problem: Creating a consistent icon means defining an identity, comparing options, and tracking decisions. Without a structured process, iterations and design choices become scattered.
overview.context: A web application where manual and integrated generation paths share the same workflow.
overview.scope: Product workflow, data, generation, billing and exports
overview.solution: Iconise connects briefs, visual directions, exploration and refinement across eight guided steps, followed by finalization. Decisions and iterations remain tied to each project.

visual.title: A usable brief
visual.description: The brief records the app, its identity and visual preferences, and guides the following steps.

visual.title: One board, nine options
visual.description: Generate or import a board of nine proposals, then select an A–I cell to continue.

visual.title: Revise without deleting
visual.description: Adjust geometry, optical perception and background; some steps can be skipped. Changing a decision marks dependent steps for review without deleting past attempts.

visual.title: Formats for the application
visual.description: Download the PNG master, a derived SVG or a favicon pack. The SVG may embed the raster image when vector tracing does not sufficiently preserve the original appearance.

architecture.description: The Next.js server verifies the session and workspace, then calls application services. Projects are persisted through Drizzle and PostgreSQL; Gemini and Stripe use separate adapters.

nodes.label: Persistence
nodes.role: Workspace-scoped projects, states and history via Drizzle

nodes.label: External generation
nodes.role: Gemini images and OpenAI creative text, flag-dependent

asyncFlows.description: Creation POST 202 → after(execute) → client status polling
Stripe → signed webhook → Stripe object replay → state and credit sync
Waitlist action → persisted jobs → SES mail worker → confirmation

decisions.title: Next.js monolith with an isolated domain
decisions.choice: Separate UI, domain services, repositories and SQL access.
decisions.rationale: This boundary keeps SQL out of components and the browser while concentrating server controls.
decisions.alternative: ADR-001 documented in the Iconise repository.

decisions.title: Manual and integrated modes in one workflow
decisions.choice: Make the iteration the shared unit for both generation paths.
decisions.rationale: The provider does not become a second workflow architecture.
decisions.alternative: ADR-002 documented in the Iconise repository.
decisions.constraint: Actual provider availability depends on external flags.

decisions.title: Stripe webhooks and append-only credits
decisions.choice: Assign credits only after replayed payment proof.
decisions.rationale: This avoids trusting a simple Checkout redirect.
decisions.alternative: ADR-002 documented in the Iconise repository.
decisions.constraint: Actual commercial activity was not verified.

decisions.title: AI provider ports and simulators
decisions.choice: Make providers replaceable without rebuilding the domain.
decisions.rationale: The domain can be tested without paid external calls.
decisions.alternative: Ports and simulators are visible in the implementation.
decisions.constraint: Tests were not executed during the audit.

decisions.title: Internationalization independent from content
decisions.choice: Separate interface language from project content language.
decisions.rationale: This preserves compatibility with projects whose content language differs.
decisions.alternative: ADR-003 documented in the Iconise repository.
decisions.constraint: The audit describes six locales; public usage remains to be confirmed.

decisions.title: Preserving iterations when going back
decisions.choice: Invalidate downstream state without irreversible deletion.
decisions.rationale: Inferred from the audited implementation: iterations remain available with a different status.
decisions.constraint: Personal rationale is not explicitly documented.

decisions.title: Multi-format icon exports
decisions.choice: Produce a derived SVG and multiple delivery resolutions.
decisions.rationale: Inferred from the audited implementation to serve favicon and web use cases.

decisions.title: Flags-controlled waitlist and opening
decisions.choice: Do not infer public availability from a deployment alone.
decisions.rationale: Inferred from the observed access configuration.
decisions.constraint: The actual launch mode remains unknown.

challenges.title: Revisiting decisions safely
challenges.problem: Changing an earlier decision may invalidate work completed in later steps.
challenges.decision: Reopen steps through status transitions, mark downstream decisions stale and preserve iterations.
challenges.solution: A transition model marks dependent steps as stale while preserving earlier iterations.
challenges.tradeoff: The added complexity requires isolated tests and review.
challenges.result: It prevents stale selections from being reused; no quantified impact is documented.

challenges.title: Keeping generation credits consistent
challenges.problem: A remote generation may fail, be retried, or produce competing updates.
challenges.decision: Combine an idempotency key, an HTTP 202 response, after() and a ledger revalidated by webhooks.
challenges.solution: Transactional reservations, idempotency keys, and conditional status transitions govern charges and refunds.
challenges.tradeoff: Production reliability was not measured in the audit.
challenges.result: The verified code contains architectural tolerance for long calls and lost responses.

challenges.title: Preserving the appearance in SVG
challenges.problem: Vectorizing a raster master may distort edges, gradients, or file size.
challenges.decision: Produce a derived SVG trace and downscale progressively for favicon formats.
challenges.solution: Vector candidates are compared against the original, with an embedded-raster fallback if needed.
challenges.tradeoff: Systematic export fidelity is not measured.
challenges.result: A derived SVG and favicon pack are provided for by the verified implementation.

challenges.title: Isolating multi-account data
challenges.problem: A project identifier sent by the browser is not proof of ownership.
challenges.decision: Resolve the session and workspace on the server, then apply relational constraints.
challenges.solution: Reads and mutations cross a central authorization boundary before repository access.
challenges.tradeoff: These controls are not a complete penetration test.
challenges.result: A workspace authorization boundary is observable in the audited code.

challenges.title: Normalizing imperfect AI output
challenges.problem: An invalid grid, empty image or badly cropped master makes downstream extraction unusable.
challenges.decision: Validate ratios, dimensions, borders and cell geometry behind a provider port.
challenges.solution: Images are validated before they enter the next workflow steps.
challenges.tradeoff: Provider success rates are not documented.
challenges.result: Several classes of unusable images can be detected before integration.

challenges.title: Keeping two languages independent
challenges.problem: The interface language should not force the generated content language for a project.
challenges.decision: Separate user.locale and projects.content_locale with an English fallback and localized routes.
challenges.solution: Interface, project content and SEO URLs can evolve independently.
challenges.tradeoff: Real-world experience and adoption were not measured.
challenges.result: Six locale catalogs and their URL strategy are defined in the audited project.

challenges.title: Launching a guarded waitlist
challenges.problem: Public signup and deferred emails create duplicate, spam and unsubscribe risks.
challenges.decision: Use action tokens, transactional persistence, leases, limits and retries.
challenges.solution: The waitlist is treated as a durable operation rather than a simple form submission.
challenges.tradeoff: Actual operation and external go-live status remain unknown.
challenges.result: The mechanisms are present in the audited sources, without evidence of public activity.

outcomes.title: Guided, versioned workflow
outcomes.description: Eight creative steps followed by finalization, with decisions and iterations preserved for each project.
outcomes.evidence: Verified in the audit: EV-003, EV-005.

outcomes.title: Configurable generation
outcomes.description: A Gemini generation path with image validation and credit handling, enabled when configured.
outcomes.evidence: Verified in the audit: EV-010 to EV-012.

outcomes.title: Export formats for apps
outcomes.description: Download the PNG master, a derived SVG that may embed the raster, and a multi-format favicon pack.
outcomes.evidence: Verified in the audit: EV-037 to EV-039.

outcomes.title: Billing and credits
outcomes.description: Generation flows can be gated by a credit and billing system.
outcomes.evidence: Verified in the audit: EV-014 to EV-016.

outcomes.title: Multilingual infrastructure
outcomes.description: Six locales are defined with a URL and fallback strategy.
outcomes.evidence: Verified in the audit: EV-023, EV-024.

limitations: The repository is private: no public GitHub CTA should be displayed.
Production mode, enabled integrations and commercial outcomes are not established.
No current authenticated product screenshot is available; this page illustration is a portfolio composition, not a product capture.
Historical ADRs mention 4×2 boards while current code uses a 3×3 board and a 4:3 target.
Tests were not executed during the audit; no green CI badge or coverage figure is published.
Coded prices must not be presented as a current commercial offer without validation.
